detail.from: The reading project's QA notes found that 39 checks were added in 5 weeks (7-10 a week) while the same defect classes kept coming back, one of them across seven separate commits, and a later formatting commit silently reverted an earlier pronunciation fix. What converged was closing a finding only when its whole class has an executable check of what the student experiences, and counting new against repeat classes in every round report. When one instance of a text-to-speech trap turned up, the rule became a census of every instance in the course file rather than assuming a one-off, and a give-away cue rule was swept over every grade.

What converged was closing a finding only when its whole class has an executable check of what the student experiences, and counting new against repeat classes in every round report. When one instance of a text-to-speech trap turned up, the rule became a census of every instance in the course file rather than assuming a one-off, and a give-away cue rule was swept over every grade. Where code can't check a class, a dated rule stands in for the check, and each check is shown to fire before the fix and runs on every lesson.

statement.from: Code gates catch broken items, not weak ones: hard-block in code only what code detects reliably, such as a broken format or key or a copied answer, keep keyword, length and wording counts advisory, and judge quality separately, since a valid shape says nothing about it.

detail.from: On 30 scored AP question sets, a stage validator passed 12 of the 14 failing sets and wrongly failed 1 of the 16 passing ones, and its results note concluded that hard gates are a safety layer, not a quality judge, since most failures were semantic rather than schema or leak failures. Its first version also hard-blocked reading-style, source-referential stems and over-blocked known passing items, so the split kept hard gates for schema, missing fields, answer leaks, extreme length and key clustering and made wording flags advisory. A separate probe of a deterministic suite on 461 generated items caught 19 of 102 failures and rejected 22 of 351 passes, and a shape-only acceptance test passed 25 of 25 in 0.006 s while a graded retest of the same service scored 8 of 20.

folded_records.detail: A prediction engine compared course designs on five synthetic student profiles; when a revised design built in five of its recommendations, the engine's next run found 2 delivered as predicted and 3 backfired (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0010-amalgamation-v2-engine-results.qmd`, line 110), and the write-up says no numerical claim in it should be trusted as a magnitude (line 120). The project's own student simulation lab calls itself a deterministic design stress test, not evidence of student outcomes (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0099-student-simulation-lab-2026-07-09.qmd`, line 23). Calibrate simulated learners against real learners once there are any.

merges.why: The simulated-students record is a special case of the broader rule. The broader rule already lists simulated students as direction for a design, never proof, with only real learners' measured outcomes as evidence. The narrower record adds three things: stress-testing a design, labelling simulated results as predictions rather than outcomes, and calibrating against real learners. Both rely on the same prediction-engine result: 2 of 5 recommendations delivered as predicted and 3 backfired. Neither record is on record, so the broader one is kept. Every other record in the slice is left as it is. Some sit close to each other but say different things: a passed gate vs research as direction, the two taught-word questions, writer context vs grounding vs rule trimming, the separate pre-reading film disagreements, and the text-dependence limits for prior knowledge, word knowledge and distractors.

merges.statement: Never pass an invented text or source off as real: use real ones, copied word for word with checkable attribution, and plainly label anything constructed, adapted, retold or machine-written.

folded_records.statement: For literature, prefer an authentic, well-written text, split into parts where needed, to fiction a model writes.
folded_records.detail: A 2026-08-19 decision in the reading project put authentic fiction first: machine-written fiction "is never going to be great", so real texts split into parts are the priority, and units built on synthetic prose were flagged as a rebuild risk (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0198-meetings-decisions-timeline-0819-1001.qmd`). The project's cold test passages are machine-written and labelled humanApproved:false, and its insight note warns never to relabel them as real (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0064-insight-stimulus-provenance-unlock.qmd`). Label any adapted, retold or machine-written text as such on the page where it is read, so no one takes it for the original or for a real source.

merges.why: Both records say a learner must never take a made-up text for a real one. Use authentic texts, and label any constructed, adapted or model-written text where it is read. The literature record is a special case of the source rule. Neither record is on record. exact-quotations is on record, but it overlaps only on word-for-word copying and its statement does not cover invented sources, so it is left alone.

merges.statement: While a student reads, show only the text, with no printed or spoken aside breaking the flow; then bring the question, remove reading help, and let them go back anytime.

folded_records.statement: Don't interrupt a text with an aside, printed or spoken, at the top of every page: it breaks the reading flow.
folded_records.detail: A review in the reading project asked for a character's interjections at the top of each page to be removed because they took away from the reading flow; they were the purpose line printed and spoken above every story part (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0230-late-sept-incidental-findings.qmd`). The ruling was to delete them: the purpose fields and their voiceovers went from five lessons, and nine clips were retired (the same file).

merges.why: An aside, printed or spoken, at the top of every page is one more thing shown besides the text while the student reads. That makes the asides record a special case of showing only the text during reading. Both protect the reading flow from interruption.

merges.statement: Questions, hints, feedback and rubrics may use only the student's version of the text so far; a word asked about must be in it, exactly or as a family form.

folded_records.statement: A word a question asks students to find, or asks about in context, must be in the text, exactly or as a family form.
folded_records.detail: A reading course enforces that a taught key word occurs in its passage, since otherwise the hunt degrades into tapping the glowing lines, and its register records a shipped task whose key word couldn't be hunted (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/artifacts/criteria-register.csv`, TOOL-10). Its QC checklist blocks any hunted word that doesn't occur in the passage exactly or by word family (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`, row B3). A baseline evaluation of a cloned course counted about 53 vocabulary items about words not in their passages (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/v2_final_package/docs/SUMMARY_AGENT.qmd`), and a question generator's prompt says never to test a word not in the passage (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/generator/g5/MCQ_REGEN_PROMPT.md`).

merges.why: A question about a word missing from the text relies on something the student's version never said. That makes the word record a special case of grounding every question, hint and feedback in the student's own text up to that point. Its exact-or-family-form allowance is kept in the statement.

merges.statement: Give each taught word or concept one complete definition of its real meaning, not an incidental property, used word for word wherever it returns, keeping words taught together distinct.

folded_records.statement: Give each taught concept one definition, used word for word wherever the concept is defined.
folded_records.detail: A red-team addendum for the reading course found one concept carrying four definitions in one lesson, on the vocabulary card, the reading goal, a level-set screen and a dose row, two of which made an incidental property part of the definition, and another concept defined only by how it is passed on, its cultural function missing from all nine content files and both video scripts. Each definition passed the standard's one-at-a-time checks, so the addendum made a single authored definition string, used verbatim at every site that defines the concept, the rule, checked mechanically, and left completeness for the age and method over property to a judge (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/feedback-2026-08-06-addendum.md`, lines 104-148). A definition must also be complete enough not to teach a different concept, and framed by what defines it, such as what a thing does, rather than a property its examples happen to share.

merges.why: Both state one rule: a single definition for each taught word or concept, used word for word everywhere it appears. The statement keeps what the folded record adds, a complete definition built on the defining feature rather than an incidental property. Neither record is on record. plain-consistent-words-for-each-step stays separate because it is about plain, jargon-free wording for procedure steps, and a-definition-in-the-words-own-form stays separate because it is about a definition's grammatical form.

merges.statement: Never point anyone reading or marking an item at what they cannot see, like an off-screen label, code, highlight or line, or the brief and source facts behind it.

folded_records.statement: Nothing a student or marker sees may refer to working material they can't see, such as the writer's brief or its numbered source facts.
folded_records.detail: A judge failed a short-answer item whose scoring notes referred to 'the brief', the research brief the writer worked from (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark_runs/analysis_iter2.md`), and an agent's review of a second generator found articles citing numbered facts from its knowledge base that the output never showed (`icloud-work/k_12_social_studies/docs/archive/OPENCLAW_HUMAN_REVIEW.md`). The writer rules forbid any reference to the brief: scoring notes must be self-contained and readable by someone who only sees the question (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/generators/saq.py`).

merges.why: Both forbid pointing a reader at something they cannot see. One covers off-screen labels, codes, highlights and lines, the other the working brief and its numbered facts, and the statement covers both. Neither is on record. words-not-line-numbers is on record and stays apart because it bans line numbers even when they are shown, since editions differ. strip-the-working-before-it-ships stays apart because it is about leftover text that is visible, not references to things that are not.

merges.statement: Write instructions a literal reader can follow: verbs match actions, units match what can be selected, and each fill-in frame stays grammatical and sensible for every possible value.

folded_records.statement: Check every fill-in frame or blank by putting in each value it may receive and reading each filled sentence for grammar and sense.
folded_records.detail: A reading-lesson QC checklist rates it high severity: a sentence frame with a learner-supplied or word-choice blank must read grammatically for every value the accept list or the learner can produce, checked by substituting each value, and an article mismatch such as 'has a enchanting' is a defect, not a copy nit (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`, line 49). A live walkthrough of a later build found an assembled sentence that carried a quoted character's first-person 'me' into the learner's own sentence (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-live-walk-2026-09-30/REGISTER.md`, line 17). The values to put in include the key, its reveal and any pronoun a quoted value brings in.

merges.why: The kept record already requires a fill-in frame to stay grammatical for every allowed answer. The folded record is that same clause written as a check: put in each value, the key and its reveal included, and read the result. Both cite the same article-mismatch frame. Neither is on record. one-answer-per-blank-and-its-size stays apart because it is about a blank having only one answer, not about grammar.

merges.statement: Use no word students may not know before the lesson teaches it, narration counting as teaching, and teach technical words directly, since context fails when the subject is new.

folded_records.statement: Teach a unit's technical words directly, before the reading, because context cannot reveal a word when the concepts around it are new too.
folded_records.detail: The Grade 3 standards breakdown names the error behind its domain-vocabulary component, working out a domain-specific word from context: a child can't use context when the whole domain is unfamiliar, because the concepts around the word are new too. The curriculum's thread map asks for each unit's technical terms to be listed in its knowledge base, taught before reading and carried with spaced recall.

merges.why: Teaching a unit's technical words before the reading is a special case of using no word before the lesson has taught it. The statement keeps the folded record's added point that technical words need direct teaching, because context cannot reveal them when the surrounding concepts are new too. Neither is on record. a-taught-word-appears-and-recurs and words-that-carry-the-knowledge (on record) stay apart because they are about which words to teach, not when.

merges.statement: Record where each field came from, not only each record, marking model-inferred content as unsourced with its reasoning, because one record can mix official text with generated fields.

folded_records.statement: Record where each field came from, not only each record: one record can mix official text with fields a model wrote.
folded_records.detail: A curriculum service tagged provenance per record, while within one record the official objective statement sat beside misconceptions and scope boundaries a model had written (`feedback_field_level_provenance.md`, `MEMORY.md`). Per-field tags then showed 43% of one course's 2,703 records with at least one model-written field, and the next training build was to keep only misconceptions not tagged as model-written; in another course the scope boundaries, misconceptions and expanded objectives were all model-written (`reference_external_ib_v253_at_10.md`). The project's standing rule was that every text field in a new corpus must trace to a primary source, with models as tools rather than authors, and that material whose source fails is dropped, not patched (`MEMORY.md`).

folded_records.statement: Record where each field of a standard's description came from, and mark anything a model inferred as having no outside source, with the reason.
folded_records.detail: The curriculum schema keys each citation by the field it backs, because a flat list forced that mapping into prose where it could drift, and it makes the source nullable but the reasoning required, since some content is inferred by a model and has no external citation. The data specification's example leaf records key concepts inferred by a model, with the assessment framework as context, because no source from the exam board defines key concepts at the per-standard level. Recording this lets anyone see what backs each claim.

merges.why: All three say provenance belongs on each field, not only on the record. The first two restate one audit (43% of 2,703 records carried a generated field). Marking model-inferred fields as unsourced, with the reasoning, is the same rule applied to a standard's description. None was on record before this run.

merges.statement: Clear the rights to every text, clip and image before building on it, since viewing rights don't cover excerpts and a withdrawn text takes everything built on it.

folded_records.statement: Clear the rights to a text before writing anything tied to its exact words, because a text withdrawn later takes every script, question and lesson built on it.
folded_records.detail: The course plan's instruction-modes spec has copyright cleared for passages before any writing anchored to their spans begins, because scripts and citation items couple to the exact text and a passage pulled after the writing loses the lesson's artifacts (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/instruction-modes-spec.md`, lines 110-112). The same spec has each theme ship its curated texts with their licensing status noted (line 99).

merges.why: One rule: clear a text's rights before building on it. Clearing a passage before writing tied to its exact words is a special case. Its reason, that a withdrawn text takes its scripts and questions with it, joins the broader record's licence caveats. Neither was on record before this run.

merges.statement: Check every scope label against the official framework before an item is made or judged, pass it explicitly and unchanged through every step, and confirm how the judge reads it.

folded_records.statement: Before judging content, check its scope labels and what the judge takes each to mean, because a wrong or misread label fails good items and looks like a content regression.
folded_records.detail: An AP run report traced zeroed accuracy and clarity scores to a grade field: the service sent "1" for Unit 1 and the judge read it as 1st grade, leaving 81 fingerprints across 1 079 evaluations. The report calls this the more dangerous of two label faults, because it lowers individual items by 10–40 pp and looks like a model regression, while the other, a subject renamed under the judge's reference lookup, zeroed every score in a run. The curriculum service's design notes record that the same standard id can appear in several courses, verified as 284 duplicate ids in one curriculum and 311 in the AP one, so a standard id alone does not settle the course. The scope labels are the subject, course, unit, grade and standard the content was made and is judged under. Pass them to the judge explicitly as given, and match a standard by its exact ID within its course.

folded_records.statement: Check a request's labels, such as course, unit and target grade, before generating or judging, and carry them unchanged through every step, never re-inferred or silently defaulted.
folded_records.detail: The project's distilled learnings rank metadata correctness as a first-tier technique: course, unit, period, standard and type must pass with authority through every generator path. A handover for the same work lists, among the techniques carried over from a sibling generator, that period metadata bugs can dominate the failure rate. Neither file gives the size of the effect. The labels also include the period and the standard's identifier, and checking them is a hard gate before tuning as well as before generating and judging.

merges.why: All three state one rule: check an item's course, unit, period, grade and standard labels before it is made or judged, and carry them explicitly and unchanged. Two cite the same benchmark fix of passing explicit labels instead of re-deriving them, and the judge-side record adds only how a judge reads a label. Matching a standard by ID within its course stays with identify-a-standard-by-its-full-place. None was on record before this run.

merges.statement: Type every prerequisite link as hard or soft and as logical, evidence-based or conventional, let only hard, non-conventional links block a learner, and invent no chains the subject lacks.

folded_records.statement: Tag every prerequisite link as logical, evidence-based or merely conventional, and let no conventional link block a learner until evidence upgrades it.
folded_records.detail: The curriculum BrainLift notes that in history and reading comprehension most ordering is designed: "A before B" is a curriculum design choice, not a logical necessity (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Curriculum & Knowledge BrainLift.md`). The assessment BrainLift, writing about AP humanities courses whose prerequisite links are shallow and sparse, says the response cannot be to force a prerequisite structure onto content that doesn't naturally have one (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/WF - Assessment  Feedback Brain - 260624-200115.md`). The reading project's curriculum reference gives every link a warrant tag, logical, empirical or conventional (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/train-teacher/references/curriculum-architecture.md`), and its instruction spec lists as an open build item an audit that classifies each hard-prerequisite link, under which a conventional one may not block the on-ramp until evidence upgrades it (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/instruction-modes-spec.md`, section 7). Never force prerequisite chains onto knowledge that has none.

merges.why: Same rule: give each prerequisite link a warrant (logical, evidence-based or conventional), let no convention-only link block a learner, and force no chains. The kept record adds hard or soft typing and fluency thresholds, so the other is a subset of it. Neither was on record before this run.

merges.statement: Choose topics or texts by an open score whose factors, weights and totals anyone can recompute, and let a person override it only with a recorded reason.

folded_records.statement: Choose topics by a transparent scoring formula people can inspect and challenge, and let a person override a score only with a stated reason.
folded_records.detail: A review of a Grade 3 reading course praised its transparent plan-first topic scoring and a reasoned human override, and the course's routing contract lists both among what to preserve (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0164-g3-v2-feedback-agent-routing.qmd`). The same review asked for the score's factors, its grade calibration and its keep, override and reject policy to be explained (the same file).

merges.why: Both say topics are chosen by an open score whose factors and weights people can recompute or challenge, and any human override carries a recorded reason. Both come from the same course review's praise of its scorecard. Neither was on record before this run.

merges.statement: Write the course sequence before items: declare its policy and feed sources to a model in order of authority, never blended, then check the order it proposes against that policy.

folded_records.statement: Give a model the sequencing policy people set and its sources in order of authority, never blended in one pass, and check its sequence against that policy.
folded_records.detail: The curriculum-architecture doctrine the reading project holds as its authority says a model asked for the best sequence without an explicit progression strategy, entry assumptions or prerequisite strictness will import whatever assumptions it happens to carry, and that feeding it standards, exams, textbooks and web content in one go is compromise, not synthesis (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0118-curriculum-architecture-brainlift-core.qmd`). Its staged order takes scope from the standards, acceptable evidence and task conditions from the assessments, and representations and examples from textbooks, which should not widen the scope without sign-off. An attempt to merge similar standards from several states into single nodes produced flattened abstractions too vague to drive lesson design (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0116-graph-architecture-brainlift-core.qmd`).

merges.why: Both rest on the same curriculum doctrine: a model asked for an order without an explicit sequencing policy brings in its own assumptions, so people set the policy first and the model's proposal is checked against it. Feeding sources in order of authority is part of that same instruction. Neither was on record before this run.

merges.statement: Before adopting or generating from curriculum sources, compare candidates item by item on content and check their facts and labels against the official framework, because derived copies shift labels.

folded_records.statement: Before adopting a source for a course's curriculum facts, compare candidate sources item by item on content and check their labels against the official framework.
folded_records.detail: A content-similarity comparison of 239 entries in a grader's bundled curriculum against the curriculum repository found 224 content matches, 218 of them under different labels, with a systematic one-period shift confirmed against the official course description (`feedback_oracle_source_reconciliation.md`). For another course the two sources sat at different levels of the framework, 39% of one with no match in the other and 99.8% of the other's atomic facts with none, so the ruling there was to merge them, and each of three courses got its own source (`MEMORY.md`, `project_oracle_session_20260501.md`).

merges.why: Both say to check curriculum sources against the official framework before relying on them, because derived copies carry shifted or misplaced labels. Comparing candidate sources item by item is that same check, made when adopting a source. Content matching in general stays with match-curriculum-data-by-content, and the two-level store stays with keep-objectives-and-cited-facts. Neither was on record before this run.

merges.statement: Fetch an item's sources and facts by its exact topic or objective, not its unit, and give the writer only the few that match, since other topics' facts blend in.

folded_records.statement: Fetch the sources for an item by its exact topic or objective, not by its broad unit or period.
folded_records.detail: The AP generator's document bank for source-based essays was indexed by course and unit, 50 entries spanning 30+ years and several topics, so a request on one topic had a 2 in 50 chance of getting documents on it, and every failing item with injected documents carried the signature of that mismatch (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/data/model_findings.md`). Matching by topic keyword first took that item type from 30% (6 of 20) to 75% (6 of 8) (the same file). Separately, the router replaced a fuzzy topic search, which sometimes returned irrelevant facts, with an exact lookup by the curriculum code each request carries, falling back to the search only when nothing matches (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/CHANGELOG.md`).

merges.why: Same AP lesson: grounding pulled by unit instead of by the item's exact topic arrives mismatched. One record says it for documents and the other for facts, and the kept one adds giving only a few. Neither was on record before this run.

merges.statement: Keep missing, ambiguous and conflicting answers, sources and rules open until one dated, named decision settles them, never inferring, averaging or widening them, and label anything built on them provisional.

folded_records.statement: When sources, rules or reviews conflict, record both as an open question and settle it in one dated, named decision, never by averaging, merging or quietly picking a side.
folded_records.detail: The reading course plans' quality library never silently deletes, merges, universalizes or promotes a source statement, and keeps a conflict open and faithful to its sources until an evidence-bound decision resolves it (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/AUTHORITY.qmd`); a snapshot does not become an accepted requirement because it was indexed (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/README.qmd`). Its conflict ledger lists each open conflict with the resolution it needs, and where a procedure's steps appear in conflicting orders, no order is enforced until it is decided (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/crosswalk/CONFLICT-LEDGER.qmd`). The requirements for an agent that builds teaching skills log a conflict between outside guidance and the project's evidence as a named tension, never silently resolved in either direction (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/train-teacher-requirements.md`). Keep every rule at the scope and source it came from, never widening it.

merges.why: Both say an open question stays marked open until an explicit, dated ruling, never inferred or quietly settled. The kept record's own source says conflicting sources stay in conflict until adjudicated, which is the whole of the other record's rule. That record's point about never widening a scoped rule is kept in the statement. Neither was on record before this run.

merges.statement: Before judging a course or assessment, declare its purpose (teaching, practice, mastery gate, diagnostic), judge it by that alone, and set pass marks only on checks that gate progress.

folded_records.statement: Before judging a course, declare what it is meant to be, a course that teaches or a practice and assessment tool, because that decides which criteria apply.
folded_records.detail: A review of the Grade 3 reading course judged it a well-built practice-and-assessment engine rather than a comprehension curriculum, and said its recommendations would be different if the course were meant as a practice app (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0081-g3-reviewer-feedback-raw-2026-07-02-reading-explorers-v2-review-verbatim.qmd`). A later evaluator gap analysis lists a declaration of product type, comprehension course or test practice, as what determines the criteria that apply (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0093-evaluator-gap-analysis-inceptbench-academics-2026-07-09.qmd`).

merges.why: Same rule: declare what a course or assessment is for before judging it, because the declared type decides which criteria apply. Both cite the same gap-analysis line on declaring product type, and the course-level record is a special case. The fuller assessment record is kept because a fold carries over only evidence, not the detail. Neither was on record before this run.

merges.statement: After any change or fix, re-run every check and quality measure on the whole set, passed items included, because a fix for one can break another.

folded_records.statement: After every change to a generator, re-measure every quality dimension, because a fix for one can break others.
folded_records.detail: The fifth benchmark run of an AP US History question generator raised the overall pass rate only from 49.6% to 53.4%, but its tables by difficulty and by dimension showed easy items fixed (27% to 68%) and hard items and cognitive demand broken (58% to 38%, 70% to 59%). The report calls it a trade-off: factual accuracy and curriculum alignment improved while difficulty alignment and cognitive demand regressed. The sweep tied this to round 2's learning 'one change at a time (9 of ~45 iterations mattered)'; this file shows what one run's changes cost, not that count.

merges.why: Both say the same thing: after a change, measure everything again because a fix for one thing can break another. Re-measuring every quality dimension after a generator change is a special case of re-running every check on the whole set. read-the-failures-not-the-average stays separate because reading failing items against the baseline is a different method.

merges.statement: Treat each defect, finding or failure as a class: repair its kind and add a standing check across everything made the same way, not just the items that failed.

folded_records.statement: Key a repair to the kind of failure, by its standard, item type and context, not to the rows that failed.
folded_records.detail: A distillation of the parallel lab's work (19 May 2026) concluded that dynamic repair works only when keyed to standard, type and context, not to benchmark row IDs, and proposed repairs keyed by substandard, standard description, type and retrieved sources rather than exact row ID. In the solver lineage that followed, repairs were written for the hidden rows that had failed, at times for a single request ID, and re-validated on those same rows: one document-question round repaired 5 of 6 failures, left 1 failing and introduced 1 new failure, and an essay round fixed rows 47 and 48 while row 49 still failed and row 27 newly failed. These records can't separate failures a repair caused from verdicts that vary between runs.

merges.why: The same rule in other words: fix the kind of failure, not the instance or the failing rows. Keying a repair to a failure's standard, item type and context is closing the class. fix-with-a-general-rule stays separate because it also keeps single-standard rules and item details out of a judge's general rubric. fix-the-source-not-only-the-copy stays separate because it says where a fix goes, not how widely it reaches.

merges.statement: Never alter an item, request or check just to raise a score: a gain from removing what a check inspects is gaming, so fix the item or harden the check.

folded_records.statement: Never change what the judge will see to suit the judge; fix the item, or the request where it was made.
folded_records.detail: A line-by-line audit of the AP generation service found code that regex-swapped words the judge penalised, deleted listed evidence that overlapped the documents and padded the gap with generic filler, silently raised easy requests to medium for three item types, rewrote one topic, and re-picked the time span a request named (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/research/inference_clean.md`). Each was ruled a crutch to remove: rewriting the text the judge scores changes the score without improving the item, and changing the request changes what the judge compares the item against. A wrong request is to be fixed where it was made, not by the generator (the same audit). Changing what the judge sees covers rewording, trimming or padding an item after it is written, and quietly altering the level, topic or period that was asked for.

folded_records.statement: A pass-rate gain that comes from removing what a check inspects is gaming the check, not better content, so treat it as a flaw in the checks to fix.
folded_records.detail: Looking back over the AP project, the reading project's knowledge base found that the multiple-choice fix once credited to real source passages did the opposite: it removed the stimulus, so the grader's leak probe was skipped. It recorded this as grader-gaming, not a provenance win. The same holds for a gain that comes from a gap in the judge's rubric. One lab's verdicts treated such a gain as fragile and second-tier rather than something to build on, unless the product's spec allows a review-drill shape.

merges.why: All three forbid moving a score without improving the item. Rewording, trimming or padding for the judge, quietly changing the requested level or topic, and removing what a check inspects are all special cases of bending content to pass a check. The kept record already asks that a fix that raises a score improved the item rather than dodged the check. tune-a-judge-to-labels-not-pass-rates stays separate because it is about calibrating a judge against labelled cases.

merges.statement: A failure that repeats across items or retries is a fault, not noise: redrafting or rescoring won't fix it, so rule out broken measurement, find its cause and test it.

folded_records.statement: Drafting several versions, retrying or rescoring evens out only random slips; a failure that recurs on every try needs its cause found and fixed.
folded_records.detail: A test that lifted document-based questions to 37 of 38 by redrafting and keeping the best left one item that was drafted 22 times across four rounds and never scored above 0.78. Its failing criterion was factual accuracy: the writer kept inserting an event from outside the period despite a guardrail against it, which the report puts down to the writer's reliability on that objective being below the threshold (`icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/exploits/EXPLOIT-008-dbq-7doc-generic-attrib.md`).

merges.why: Both say a failure that recurs is a systematic fault, not random noise, and needs its cause found. Saying that redrafting, retrying or rescoring only evens out random slips is the same claim seen from the side of the remedy. find-the-cause-in-the-failing-items and find-what-every-run-shared stay separate because they name different pitfalls: a shared field that is not the cause, and a ceiling that comes from something every run shared.

merges.statement: Before choosing a fix or calling a change a gain, break results down by item type, unit and failure kind, and apply changes only where they help: averages hide losses.

folded_records.statement: Test each added stage, or background given to a writer, on each item type, and apply it only where it measurably helps, since an average can hide losses.
folded_records.detail: An agent's notes from one day of the AP work record that the retrieval-heavy pipeline scored 90.4% on the essay type against 100% for the model alone, and 83.7% against 86% on the short-answer type, while the two source-based types needed its source injection (+58.6 and +20.9 points); the plan was to bypass the pipeline for the two free-response types. Separately, a fallback directive that helped document-based items (4 of 5) regressed two other types when added for all 25 items, and the lab's verdict was to use it per objective only, never globally (`BEAD_EVIDENCE_INDEX.md`). An addition that lifts one item type can lower another.

folded_records.statement: Before tuning a generator, record why each failed attempt failed, by kind, instead of one pass-or-fail flag.
folded_records.detail: An assessment of the reading project's question generator found 51% of attempts ending as an opaque `generated_item:null`, and its first priority, validating the evaluation harness before trusting any number, includes instrumenting why each one died (topic reject, format failure or truncation) before tuning (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/courses/g5-reading/analysis/GENERATOR_ASSESSMENT.md`, line 76). The same line asks for failures to be bucketed by type rather than one boolean, citing an earlier AP effort's lessons, and notes that effort burned weeks "stuck at 28%" on four harness bugs.

merges.why: Testing an added stage type by type, because the average hides a type it lowers, is breaking results down by item type before calling a change a gain, and it gives the same reason. Recording why each failed attempt failed, by kind, before tuning is the breakdown by failed criterion before choosing a fix. read-the-failures-not-the-average stays separate because it reads individual items against the baseline rather than breaking down counts.

merges.statement: Test each change alone against an equally informed control on the same fixed items and conditions, differing only in that change, and adopt it only on a net gain.

folded_records.statement: Judge a tuned or edited model against the same model given the same instructions, sources and output budget, and keep the simpler baseline unless the change beats it.
folded_records.detail: An experiment plan asks whether an edited model improves context-sensitive judgment beyond an equally informed prompt, calls a null result valid, and keeps the prompt-only baseline as the default if the edited model fails (`uae-education-ai/HERETIC_PLAN.md`). An earlier design gives a fine-tuned judge the same prompt, rule text, source access, decoding settings and output budget as the prompted base it is compared with (`uae-education-ai/EVALUATION.md`). Neither comparison had been run.

folded_records.statement: Replay each new automatic filter on its own over saved, already-judged items, and adopt it only if the replay shows a net gain.
folded_records.detail: Replayed over 150 saved, graded rows, a bundle of code filters placed before a model selector lowered the pass rate from 91.3% to 87.3% and cut hard question sets from 10/10 to 3/10. Each filter was plausible alone, but together they over-rejected valid candidates. The fix was never to ship the bundle and to add a filter only if its own replay shows a net gain of at least 3 rows.

merges.why: An equally informed baseline (same instructions, sources and output budget) is a control that differs only in the tuning. Replaying each new filter on its own over saved, already-judged items is testing one change against fixed items. Both add the rule that a change is kept only if it beats the control. isolated-gains-may-not-stack, confirm-the-change-actually-fired and test-and-prune-a-writers-rules stay separate because they cover combinations, whether a change ran, and pruning.

merges.statement: Nothing that wrote, picked or was optimised against an item certifies it: confirm with an uninvolved check from another model family on fresh cases, and read unshared gains as gaming.

folded_records.statement: When a score picks among candidates, confirm the pick with a separate check on cases it wasn't picked on, because a pick can game the score that made it.
folded_records.detail: Round 2 found this in the AP work, with its own evidence. The deep sweep adds an experiment plan that runs 12 candidate edits on 48 search inputs, confirms only the top 2 on 48 separate selection inputs, chooses the winner once on those scores, and lets no unvalidated model judge choose an edit (`uae-education-ai/HERETIC_PLAN.md`). Its selection scores come from mechanical checks and blind human scoring, so the plan avoids the gaming risk rather than measuring it.

merges.why: Confirming a pick on cases it wasn't picked on, because a pick can game the score that made it, is a special case of the rule that nothing which picked an item certifies it, that confirmation runs on fresh items, and that a gain the independent check doesn't share is gaming. The kept record's own example is a pick that gamed its grader. Neither record was on record. Re-grading for noise and best-of-N grader validation stay separate because they are different rules.

merges.statement: Let a grader pick only among drafts passing the code checks, after showing on saved candidates that it tracks the real criterion and beats taking the first valid one.

folded_records.statement: Let a model judge choose only among items that pass the code checks, and keep it as a selector only if it beats taking the first valid item.
folded_records.detail: Selector calibration on saved AP candidates found that when invalid candidates reached the model selector, a fluent but invalid question set could beat the one that actually passed, so the rule became code filters first, with the model a selector and not a rescue path. On one saved archive of 15 rows the model selector passed 13, the same as taking the first valid candidate, so it was kept audit-only until a larger calibration proves a lift. The best possible pick also passed 13, so that archive could not show a lift either way.

merges.why: Both statements give the same test for a selector: it may pick among drafts only once it beats taking the first valid one on saved candidates. The model-judge record is one case of a grader picking, and it adds that the pick happens only among drafts that pass the code checks. The new statement keeps that point. Neither record was on record.

merges.statement: Keep a question only when solvers outside the generator's model family all fail it blind and answer it with the text, failure there often meaning ambiguity or a broad key.

folded_records.statement: Before checking whether a solver can answer an item without its text, check that it can with the text, since failing there often means ambiguity or a broad key.
folded_records.detail: In a Grade 5 generation run, every keeper had to be solved with the passage by a model from another family and not recovered without it; 735 of 1,152 written items passed the with-text control, and the 417 failures were often ambiguity or broad keying rather than leakage (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0091-g5-question-generation-retrospective-codex-2026-07-09.qmd`). In another tranche the control-pass rate did not predict blind certification: 98.9% of single-choice items passed the control, but only 46.1% of those were certified blind. The run's rules say to always run the with-text control before blind certification, and the reading leak schema passes an item only when its with-passage correct rate is at least 0.80 and its without-passage rate no more than 0.15 above chance (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0243-generator-quality-schema-cluster-2026-07.qmd`).

merges.why: The with-text check is the second half of the blind-and-with-text rule. The kept record already carries the same run's evidence: 417 of 1,152 items failed the with-text control, those failures were often ambiguity, and passing the control didn't predict passing blind. The statement adds that diagnosis. Neither record was on record. The low-confidence, hard-way and student-level leak records stay separate because each sets a different rule for running or counting the blind check, and the student-level one pulls the other way on low-confidence guesses.

merges.statement: Besides checking that a quote is exact, check that the passage itself states everything the claim says, not merely that the claim is plausible, and audit 'partly supported' verdicts.

folded_records.statement: A quotation can be exact and still not support the answer it backs, so check separately that the evidence covers everything the answer claims.
folded_records.detail: In one reading lesson a modelled write-up's answer required sunlight, carbon dioxide and water, while the quotation it revealed named only sunlight and carbon dioxide, so the model asserted more than its evidence showed; the scripted audit doesn't compare a revealed quote with the revealed answer. A draft evaluation design for an AI judge checks in code that each quotation is an exact substring of the fragment, then has people working blind rate separately whether it supports the verdict and rule, from 0 (absent or misleading) to 2 (sufficient and faithful).

merges.why: Both say a claim counts as supported only when the cited text itself states all of it. In one, an exact quote backed an answer that named three things while the quote named two. In the other, a span labelled fully supported added a fact the paragraph never states. Neither record was on record. Tracing generated text to source facts stays separate as a rule for generating.

merges.statement: Accept a right answer nobody planned for, but only when the judge is sure, and log it for review.

folded_records.statement: Mark an answer that goes beyond the plan on whether it holds together rather than on whether it matches the planned list, so going further is never punished.
folded_records.detail: A built Grade 3 lesson scores its "and what else?" stretch question deliberately generously: any sensible answer earns full credit with no further ask, because the beat rewards thinking beyond the first answer and must never punish it. Its cross-text question lets a child name any story they know, and the rubric judges whether the answer holds together, never whether the story is recognised, rewarding noticing differences above matching the planned list. Neither rule says how sure a judge must be before giving that credit. Such an answer may be a further idea or the student's own example.

merges.why: Marking an answer that goes beyond the planned list on whether it holds together, not on matching the list, is the same rule as accepting a right answer nobody planned for. The on-record record already cites the same walkthrough quotes on judging whether the answer holds together and on rewarding more than matching the list. It was on record, so its statement stays as it is.

merges.statement: Before believing a score, high or low, check the harness, scorer and items that produced it, and when results look uniform or mostly flagged, suspect the check before the content.

folded_records.statement: Before trusting a score, check what produced it: the scorer, where every item came from, and whether judge, model and bar match across conditions.
folded_records.detail: An AP question-generator project's score, described as stuck at ~28%, was largely a measurement artifact of four harness bugs: a wrong field read, a grader on the wrong host, one question type mis-routed (0→0.77 once fixed) and truncated essay output. In the reading project, a dev server with no scoring credentials produced 11 phantom FAILs because nobody checked the scoring API first. A note linking the AP case to a Grade 3 analogue states the rule: prove the gate measures what it claims before trusting any verdict. Check that the scorer is live, reads the right field, runs on the right host and sees the whole output. Check that every item came from the system under test, with the change under test switched on, by the path it ships in, not from a bank, cache, fallback or mock.

folded_records.statement: When a check flags much of what it checks, suspect the check before the content and confirm its flags against the material.
folded_records.detail: In the reading project, an onset-audibility check flagged 31 of 123 clips, all falsely, because it measured loudness from the universal 0.28s lead-in instead of the detected start of speech, and a detector firing on 25% of clips at random was itself the sign that the check was broken (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0200-content-audio-review-traps.qmd`). A course auditor failed 81/81 item banks against a >=15 depth constant hard-coded in the auditor itself, which the specification only quoted; against the real floor of 8, 79/81 passed and 2 fell genuinely short (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0235-g5-course-build-pipeline-2026-06-23-to-06-30.qmd`). A lesson walker went from v10.1 to v10.16, each version fixing a false negative in the walker itself, never by loosening an assertion (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0222-g3-l4-l1-parity-rebuild-2026-09-17-to-21.qmd`), and test pins are re-set only for what the diff attributes to the content, never loosened (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0199-engineering-git-gate-traps.qmd`). Examine where a check's threshold came from and what it measures from, and fix the checker rather than loosen an assertion to get a pass.

merges.why: Same learning: verify what produced a score before believing it. The harness record lists the same checks (live scorer, right fields, items from the shipping path) and comes from the same case of four harness bugs. Suspecting the check when nearly everything is flagged repeats the instrument record's closing rule.

merges.statement: Report a pass rate over every requested item from live verdicts only, keeping errored, unrun or cached checks and other pipeline failures apart from content failures, none dropped.

folded_records.statement: Count a pass or a fail only where a live judge returned a verdict on the very item delivered, and report calls with no verdict apart.
folded_records.detail: In the AP generator work, a baseline of 0.8667 was cited across five-plus memos, final verdicts among them, with no file behind it, and the only result file for a score cited as a collapse came from a run that took 8 ms because the harness sent empty prompts (`icloud-work/aptraining/THELOOP.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining/handover/2026-05-01T1039Z_main_session_close/01_HANDOVER.md`). A run promoted as 100% fresh carried records rated as passes predicted from cached neighbours, with the live judge skipped, in the first three of its 50 records that were read; an earlier version's 100% included 4 passes served from cached content; and a cache-backed solver's pass rate roughly equalled its cache hit rate (`icloud-work/aptraining/artifacts/validated/2026-05-23T0840Z_den_solver_v10_STRICT_FRESH_K4/VALIDATION_REASON.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining/artifacts/validated/2026-05-23T0840Z_den_solver_v10_STRICT_FRESH_K4/den_solver_acceptance_20260523T082319Z.jsonl`; `icloud-work/aptraining/artifacts/second_tier/2026-05-22T1830Z_den_solver_v2_online_K_N_with_cache/SECOND_TIER_REASON.md`). Errors were counted the other way: 4,800 authentication failures were logged as per-item scoring errors, 29 auto-zeroed scoring errors in 150 most likely pulled one item type 26.7 points below a parallel run, and a grader timeout marked rows 0.0 that had already passed, so a later backlog splits failures into infrastructure, format, content and variety before any pass rate (`icloud-work/aptraining/helpers/data/.agent/memory/feedback_check_score_phase_duration.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining/coordination/RESULTS.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/full-copy/parallel-ideas-lab/reports/SELECTOR_CALIBRATION_TAKEAWAYS_20260520.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/evidence/FUTURE_RUN_IMPROVEMENT_BACKLOG_20260521.md`). In the reading project's test design, numbers drifted between documents (0.930 against 0.928), which is why its gate on what may be claimed lives in code (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0080-map-proxy-case-for-approval-2026-07-02-incept-map-proxy-approval-package.qmd`). A call or check that errored, timed out, returned unreadable output or never ran is no verdict. The completion rate goes beside the pass rate, and such a call is re-run rather than left to pass or fail in silence.

folded_records.statement: Report a pass rate over everything requested, keep failed outputs in the denominator, and give any rate that leaves errors out only beside it.
folded_records.detail: One benchmark run lost 39 of 120 requested items to generation errors and computed its 49.4% pass rate on the 81 that came back (`icloud-work/evaluator/docs/reports/BENCHMARK_RUN8_REPORT.md`). Another report counted 11 judge errors against its headline rate of 61.1% but dropped them from its per-type rates, so a type with 7 errors among 11 items showed 100% (`icloud-work/evaluator/docs/reports/evaluation_20260225_155759_209babe7.md`). A later runner counts generation failures as zeros (`icloud-work/evaluator/benchmark_official.py`). The report states what happened to each item: passed, failed, malformed, never produced or not judged.

merges.why: One rule for an honest pass rate. The pipeline record already says to count each failure and drop none, which is the requested-item record. It also keeps tool failures apart from content failures, which is the real-verdict record.

merges.statement: Count banks and rates by distinct, independently certified items per type, not rows, which hide repeats, treating an item's variants as that item and keeping them in one split.

folded_records.statement: Count a bank or a run by its distinct items that passed independent checks, per item type, because row and pass counts hide a generator that repeats itself.
folded_records.detail: An independent inventory of an AP corpus found 143,026 gross rows but 49,571 sampling-eligible exact unique candidate bodies and 0 independently certified rows, and rejected the claim of 100,000 unique usable samples. In the reading project's self-audit, a bank's 8,937 passes included no sequence or match item that survived strict QA, and one template had been stamped 1,475 times. The spread of sources and stems is checked as well.

merges.why: Same rule in other words, drawn from the same inventory case: count a bank or run by its distinct, independently certified items, not by its rows.

merges.statement: Claim a rate or a difference only from a sample sized to show it, with the count reported, and a difference only once it clears the judge's run-to-run spread.

folded_records.statement: Count a difference between versions as real only when it clears the judge's run-to-run spread for that item type, measured by re-scoring the same saved items over several runs.
folded_records.detail: A three-run probe of the AP judge on unchanged outputs found a standard deviation of 1.54 points overall but 7-9 points on the document-based type, with two types not varying at all, and the same outputs scored 24/30 and 19/30 on two runs, so a difference under 5 points from a single call was not to be trusted (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/MEMORY.md`). A routed setup's 92% rested on one lucky 30/30 run of one item type whose rate over three seeds was about 80%, and an earlier single-run score in the 0.9 range proved to be noise when re-run over three seeds (the same file; `icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/BEADS.md`). The project then required three seeds before any single-attempt number, a standard deviation across seeds of 4 points or less before a mean could be read, and an audit of the prompt and output of anything that passed unexpectedly (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/PLAN.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/PILLARS_2026_05_12.md`). Measure the spread item by item, and audit an unexpected win as closely as a loss.

folded_records.statement: Report the count behind every rate and claim or change only what it can show, never acting on one run over a handful of items.
folded_records.detail: AP benchmark run reports set format-routing rules from format-by-difficulty cells of 5 to 15 items, and the same cell flipped from run to run: easy matching items read 15% on 13 items in Run 3, where the report proposed routing them to another format, 0% on 6 items in Run 4, and 64% in Run 5 (`APinceptbench/docs/reports/BENCHMARK_RUN3_REPORT.md`, `APinceptbench/docs/reports/BENCHMARK_RUN4_REPORT.md`, `APinceptbench/docs/reports/BENCHMARK_RUN5_REPORT.md`). A reading assessment's plan limits a pilot of about 40 students to usability, engagement and early item red flags, with no calibration claims, and sets kill criteria that are meaningful at that size, such as session completion of at least 90% (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/README.md`, `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/04_CONCURRENT_VALIDITY_PLAN.md`). Because adaptive selection rarely serves the extreme items, that pilot recruits learners at both ends on purpose, and an adversarial review called at least eight per end fine for feasibility but not tail validation (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/00_AUDITS_AND_FIXES.md`, `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_FINDINGS.md`). No verdict rests on fewer than about 10 items and no rate on fewer than about 30, and acting here means routing, restricting, redesigning or dropping an item type.

merges.why: The sample-size record already contains the noise rule: a difference counts only when it clears the judge's run-to-run spread. 'Small samples, small claims' is the same sizing rule seen from the other side.

merges.statement: A verdict holds only for the pinned model version that gave it, so compare runs under one version and, when it changes, re-score everything, baseline and blind solves included.

folded_records.statement: Compare judged scores only when the same pinned judge version scored every run, and when the judge changes, re-score everything, the baseline included.
folded_records.detail: In the AP project, the same generated items scored 63.64% under one judge version and 89.56% under the next, a 25.92-point swing from the judge alone (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/MEMORY.md`); a model recorded at 90.67% re-scored about 54.7% after a later judge update (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/feedback_iterative_improvement_not_fresh_models_2026_05_12.md`); and one setup scored 70.0% on one judge instance and 62.89% on another (`icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/full-copy/aptraining-root/plan.md`). A stored baseline also differed from a fresh run of the same model on the same prompts, 0.9475 against 0.9307, and several regressions became lifts or ties once the baseline was re-run (the memory file; `icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/BEADS.md`). Versions whose weights never changed were reported 4.4 to 8.2 points below a stored 68.22% (the plan file). The rule became to name the judge version with every pass rate and compute no difference across versions, and the eval template records the version (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent-v2/templates/eval-cycle.md`). Act on a judged score only when every run was scored under the same conditions and each score traces to stored per-item verdicts; record the judge version with every score, and re-score rather than reuse a stored number.

merges.why: Same rule: a judged result is valid only for the pinned model version that produced it. So old verdicts are re-run and the baseline is re-scored when that version changes.

merges.statement: Measure and headline a generator on one attempt per input fixed in advance, per item type, in the mode that ships, on untuned topics, reporting retried or best-of-several rates apart.

folded_records.statement: Measure a generator on one attempt per item in the mode that ships, at topics it was never tuned on, because tuned topics or a best-of-several pick overstate it.
folded_records.detail: In an exploit study, a prompt set tuned on 17 topics passed 32 of 33 items there and 0 of 50 on fresh topics, and was quarantined; an earlier 50-of-50 result failed a fresh re-test of 50 at 10.00%. A strict one-call harness put a fine-tuned model at 13% one-shot, where an earlier 83.3% had been inflated by what the note calls inference crutches. Headline the first-attempt rate on fresh topics in the shipping mode, not a tuned or best-of-several figure.

merges.why: Same rule: headline a generator on one fixed first attempt per input in the mode that ships. Retries and best-of-several picks are reported apart because they overstate it.

merges.statement: Count fixes, gains or checks as proven only on fresh held-out items written apart from whoever built them, kept from tuning, training and repair, never rerun to chase a pass.

folded_records.statement: Keep held-out items away from any tuning or repair, and count a claimed gain only once it is re-tested on fresh items its author never saw.
folded_records.detail: An AP solver's first hidden run scored 37 of 50, and its shared failure classes drove targeted repairs, with cache entries prewarmed for them and replays of the earlier failures rising from 4 of 13 to 13 of 13; the repair note itself expected about 50 of 50 on the same failure mix. Both runs later promoted as validated at 50 of 50 read the same hidden file, item-type lanes were re-validated on the same rows 50-99 after repairs aimed at those rows, and repair probes ran directly on files of the hidden failure rows. On fresh rows 100-149, one attempt per item, the stack scored 239 of 250 and a new failure family appeared, and a ten-item public set patched to 10 of 10 failed one of a two-item sample. Held-out items stay out of any cache or item pool as well, the final test is never rerun to chase a pass, and no set is reused round after round.

folded_records.statement: Keep every evaluation item out of a writer's training data, and check for overlap against every held-out file, the grader's reference set included, before each training run.
folded_records.detail: The grader's bundled regression set was kept as reference only, because training on it would be direct test contamination (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/reference_oracle_helper.md`). A data-selection plan required a new pool to have zero overlap with the 297-prompt held-out set before grading it (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/research_grape_data_selection_v28.md`), and the best early training recipe used only records excluded from the held-out set (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/project_v8_best.md`).

folded_records.statement: Test a check on cases written apart from whoever built it, with the expected outcomes fixed before the first run.
folded_records.detail: In the reading course, a visibility detector passed its own 48 controls but missed 10 of 18 cases written independently, whose expected outcomes had been fixed before the first measurement; after cause-level repairs it passed all 48 and all 18 unchanged (`grade3-reading/artifacts/codex-qa/experience-2026-09-14/RESULT.md`, `grade3-reading/artifacts/codex-qa/experience-2026-09-14/independent-observer/REVIEW.md`). The plan for an automated repair loop keeps the acceptance files outside what the repairing model can write, and requires that its commands can write only a proposal folder, never the source, judge, contract or evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/codex-qa/controller-2026-09-14/PLAN.md`). An assessment of the earlier tools notes that hashes give no protection against a writer that can change both a result and its evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/codex-qa/tool-reuse-assessment-2026-09-14.md`). Keep those cases, the judge and the evidence out of reach of whatever writes the fix.

merges.why: All four are the held-out rule: evidence for a fix, gain or check counts only on items that played no part in making it. Keeping those items out of training and out of reach of whatever writes the fix are special cases of it.

merges.statement: Label every number and claim with what produced it, its grader, version, attempts, sample, scope and evidence class, and word the claim no more strongly than that evidence covers.

folded_records.statement: Tag every claim with how it was established, keep that label beside the number, and word the claim no more strongly than the check covers.
folded_records.detail: The course standard's practice layer says claims are licensed by instruments and nothing else, and names the instrument behind each claim (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`). Its golden checklist keeps authored, mechanically validated, runtime verified, human accepted, production verified and outcome validated as distinct states (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/2.0.0/GOLDEN-CHECKLIST.qmd`, Q003). The course-plan agents tag every shipped claim verified, asserted or open and never silently promote one (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/course-formula-agents.md`), and a video rubric tags its operating heuristics so that none is cited as a proven learning threshold (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/video-red-team/references/rubric.md`). The ways a claim can be established include being measured on your own items, simulated, derived, taken from a study, decided or asserted.

merges.why: Both put a label beside every number saying where it came from. The evidence class is one of the fields the number record already lists, and wording a claim no more strongly than its evidence follows from that label.

merges.statement: Report every result as measured on real output, misses included and never rounded across its bar, recomputed from primary records; a projected, templated or summary-copied figure is no result.

folded_records.statement: Derive every number, verdict and claim in a report fresh from the primary records at the time of writing, never from summary prose or an intermediate report.
folded_records.detail: A self-audit of the reading project found that its synthesized briefing had drifted ahead of the certified compliance files into a rosier story: it reported the course as passing on a course id found in no knowledge entry and no compliance file, while the certified file recorded 3 FAIL / NOT MET, and the fix was to regenerate views from the certified files and never cite a pass that no file on disk backs (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0069-self-audit-insights.qmd`). The course graph's metadata had said 5 edge types where its build script and schema define four (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0122-g3-reading-course-graph.qmd`). A judge-calibration report was recomputed from the raw per-call records rather than trusted from the run harness's own summary (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0243-generator-quality-schema-cluster-2026-07.qmd`). That covers structured results as well as primary records, rules out templated text and notes as sources, and means citing no figure without a record behind it.

folded_records.statement: Claim an improvement only from a scored run of real output; projected gains, mock tests and result templates still waiting to be filled in are not results.
folded_records.detail: A pipeline's build log put its pass rate at '99% (projected)' and its validation at 'Mock tests: 95% passing (22/23 tests)' (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/AGENT3_EXECUTION_LOG.md`), its README gave per-layer 'Result' figures (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/README.md`), and its deployment test record still read '[PENDING - To be filled after deployment]' (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/DEPLOYMENT_TEST_RESULTS.md`). A later live comparison of six pipelines rated it at 0% reliability, its six validation layers 'not functioning' (`icloud-work/incept/nova_forge/PIPELINE_EVALUATION.md`).

merges.why: All three say a reported figure must be a real measurement traced to primary records. A projected gain or an unfilled template is the unmeasured case; a number copied from a summary is the untraced one.

merges.statement: Test a claim across everything it covers, every lesson, unit, standard, bank and population, not a showcase or convenient slice, reporting the share that holds and what went unchecked.

folded_records.statement: Judge a course on all its delivered lessons, not the reviewed or showcase one: re-derive each quality claim across every lesson and report the share that holds.
folded_records.detail: In a Grade 3 reading course, the lesson that had already been reviewed was the polished one: real modelling of rejecting the alternative held in 1 of 18 lessons by one count and 3 of 18 by another, with the reviewed lesson among them (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/SKILL.md`, rule 8; `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`, section L). In a later round the lesson under review had its passage from a showcase build rather than the generator, so findings about its shape did not generalise (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/feedback-2026-08-06-addendum.md`, §D). The rule since is to recompute every interaction-quality claim across all lessons and report the fraction that holds, and the course standard adds that unreviewed content cannot inherit a strong sample's result and asks for a manifest of what was and wasn't checked (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/2.0.0/GOLDEN-CHECKLIST.qmd`, Q006). Say what was checked, what wasn't and what was left out.

merges.why: Judging a course on every delivered lesson rather than the reviewed showcase one is a special case of measuring across everything a claim covers rather than a convenient slice.

merges.statement: Report the mean score beside the pass rate, fixing in advance which decides, because a pass cut turns small shifts near the bar into noise or false gains.

folded_records.statement: Compare versions on the averaged continuous score as well as the pass rate, because a pass/fail cut turns small score shifts into apparent noise or false gains.
folded_records.detail: An analysis of the AP judge's scores found that its 0.85 pass threshold caused most of the apparent run-to-run variance and that the averaged continuous score was about five times sharper at no extra cost; on it, a version that gained 1.77 points on pass rate had lost 0.88, and the document-based type's noise was nearly all an artefact of the threshold (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/MEMORY.md`). Decision rules written before the next run required reporting both the pass rate and the continuous score, type by type (`icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/full-copy/aptraining-root/v38_decision_rules.md`).

merges.why: Same rule in other words: report the continuous mean beside the pass rate, because the pass cut turns small shifts near the bar into noise or false gains.

merges.statement: Set each pass or leak bar above the item's chance score, computed from how the live system scores it, and within what the judge can reliably reach, never near-perfect.

folded_records.statement: Compute each item's guessing floor from how the live system scores it, and count a leak only when answers without the text beat that floor by a wide margin.
folded_records.detail: A live probe of a course's own server scorer found that select-two items authored as single-answer paid full credit whenever the first pick was right, which put their guessing floor at about 0.167 instead of 0.015, an order of magnitude higher (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/artifacts/scoring-rule-probe-2026-07-10/scoring-rule-probe.md`). The calibration that followed made it a standing rule to compute floors per item from its response declaration, never from the format label (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/artifacts/g3-control-set-2026-07-10/G3-CALIBRATION-REPORT.md`). Ordering items certified against one seeded shuffle were re-probed under many and 72 were decertified (`~/Projects/grade3-reading/artifacts/wiki-research/cross-cutting.md`), and the bar became at least 8 shuffles for ordering and selection items, with any threshold at least 0.20 above the item's floor. Test ordering and selection items without their text under many shuffles, not one.

merges.why: The guessing-floor record is the lower half of the bar record: both put a leak bar above the item's chance score as the live system actually scores it.

merges.statement: Score a judge on labelled cases per kind of fault, counting misses and false alarms against a baseline that always gives the majority verdict, with its bar from human agreement.

folded_records.statement: When scoring a model's rule decisions, report how often it catches the rare decision, against a baseline that always gives the common one.
folded_records.detail: The decision-bank experiment design computes, before any model call, a per-rule modal-decision prior and an always-modal baseline, and reports per-rule macro-F1 and minority-decision recall so class imbalance cannot pass for obedience to the contract. Its semantic ceiling is the agreement independent people reach before adjudication, and its decision floor is that ceiling minus a separately preregistered margin.

merges.why: Same rule: when labels are mostly one class, raw accuracy hides a judge that misses the rare one. So both report misses per class against a baseline that always gives the common verdict.

merges.statement: Learn and report what a judge or gate actually does from its code and saved verdicts, tested on a few items, not from documentation or a published description.

folded_records.statement: Describe and report a quality gate from the code that ran and the verdicts it saved, not from its documentation, because the two drift apart.
folded_records.detail: The quiz generator's README promises 0-10 scores, a repair whenever a check scores below 7, and up to 3 attempts. In the code a check passes on score >= 1, the live loop makes one repair call (19 of 60 saved items are such rewrites), and the three-attempt function is defined but never called. A debug line forces the first distractor to pass whenever all fail the plausibility check, so that check could never reject an easy item, and all 23 failure records hold an empty repair list because repairs are saved under another key. The same drift appears elsewhere in scope: the item benchmark's README lists a 'Giveaway answers' rule that its rules file does not contain, and the evaluator's plan says 'exact ID lookup only' while its curriculum search still falls back to search.

merges.why: Both say an evaluator is what its code does, not what its documentation or label claims, so learn about it and report on it from its source and its saved verdicts.

merges.statement: Measure the depth mix of generated questions, such as the share needing reasoning rather than recall, as its own figure against a target, since generators skew and accuracy hides it.

folded_records.statement: Measure how many questions need reasoning rather than recall as a figure of its own, because a set can score near-perfect on accuracy and alignment and still lean on recall.
folded_records.detail: A benchmark of 1,030 generated Arabic questions gave near-perfect curriculum alignment (10.0) and factual accuracy (9.96) but 6.76/10.0 on inference and pedagogy, and found that the questions tended toward rote recall (`icloud-work/incept/ML_TRAINING_INSIGHTS_REPORT.md`). In a 50-question AP evaluation, cognitive demand failed 35 times, described as questions that test recall rather than higher-order thinking (`icloud-work/incept/workflow/reports/REPORT_20260223_144619.md`), and an AP benchmark rejects recall-only stems such as "What year..." before scoring (`icloud-work/incept/README.md`). Hand reviews of written Grade 3 lessons found the same: every visible read-the-text question in one lesson was literal recall, and all 9 reading checks in another were (`shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U2-L1-main-review.md`, `shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U1-L12-review.md`).

merges.why: The share of questions needing reasoning rather than recall is one reading of the depth mix. Both make depth a figure of its own because generators skew and other scores hide it.

merges.statement: Prove a generator on every item type, scope, grade and difficulty it will serve, accepting it on its worst, since success on one shows nothing about another.

folded_records.statement: Test a generator on every item type it must produce and accept it on its worst type, not its average, since one type's score can hide another's failure.
folded_records.detail: In the AP project, one model's reported numbers came from multiple-choice items only; on the full ten-cell test, its document-based outputs failed to parse 50% of the time, 13/30 and 17/30 in the two courses (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/research/OVERNIGHT_RECAP.md`). The project then set its goal as the minimum over its ten course and item-type cells, not the mean, because an average can hide a regression on the hardest cell (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/NORTH_STAR.md`).

merges.why: The same rule on two axes: success on one item type or scope says nothing about another, so each must pass on its own. Accepting on the worst type is that rule written as a bar.

merges.statement: Change a check only after a paired trial on frozen scenarios shows a gain and no new misses, even when just adding reference text, which can make a judge worse.

folded_records.statement: Adding reference passages to a general judge's prompt can make it worse at catching factual errors and less consistent; compare it with and without them before adopting them.
folded_records.detail: In one experiment an item evaluator's main judge was given Wikipedia passages in its prompt: it caught 3 of 22 factual errors, down from 6 of 22 without them, and its variance rose to 7.0% from 5.5%, so the change was reverted (`icloud-work/inceptbench/docs/EVALUATOR_VARIANCE_FIX.md`, deleted in commit e5be84f).
